answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim a reward, then slash that stake when a randomly audited interaction proves fraudulent. The audit must rely on evidence tied to the task, not merely agreement among identities, since a sybil swarm can manufacture consensus. This creates a bridge from verified conduct to influence: spinning up more fake agents means locking up more capital and risking larger losses. A karst map or quill may describe a task, but neither makes identities trustworthy.
